explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang phrase used when someone exposes another person's past embarrassing or damaging information (often on social media), causing humiliation or reputational harm.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢俾人炒白底，啲舊相同啲短片全部畀人放上網，依家好難做人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 caau2 baak6 dai2, di1 gau6soeng2 tung4 di1 dyun2pin2 cyun4bou6 bei2 jan4 fong3 soeng5 mong5, ji4gaa1 hou2 naan4 zou6jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被人炒白底，舊照片和短片全部被放上網，現在很難做人。
examples.english_sentence: He had his past exposed; his old photos and videos were all posted online, and now he's having a hard time.

mandarin_meaning: 炒米 / 爆米（以米為原料炒/爆成的零食）
english_meaning: puffed rice; popped rice snack (rice kernels roasted/popped into a crunchy snack)
explanation_mandarin: 「炒米」在廣東話中多指把米粒經過乾炒或加熱處理而成的脆米小吃（類似爆米花或米花）。在某些地區也會在祭祀或節慶時見到炒米作為供品或零食。注意它與「炒飯」不同，後者是以熟米飯再翻炒而成。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "炒米" usually refers to rice grains that have been dry-roasted or popped into a crunchy snack (similar to popped or puffed rice). It can also appear as an offering or snack during certain festivals. It is distinct from "fried rice" (炒飯), which is cooked rice stir-fried with other ingredients.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺街市買咗包炒米，返屋企當零食食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gaai1 si5 maai5 zo2 baau1 caau2 mai5, faan1 uk1 kei2 dong3 ling4 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在街市買了一包炒米，回家當零食吃。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a bag of puffed rice at the market and ate it as a snack at home.

mandarin_meaning: 炒米饼（膨化或油炸的米制零食）
english_meaning: puffed/fried rice cake or rice cracker (snack)
explanation_mandarin: 一種以米為原料，經過膨化或油炸製成的脆餅，常見的零食，口感酥脆，通常有不同風味或調味。
explanation_english: A snack made from rice that is puffed or fried into a crunchy cake or cracker. Commonly eaten as a snack and available in various flavors.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我好鍾意食炒米餅，細個嗰陣成日買嚟當零食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6 caau2 mai5 beng2, sai3 go3 go2 zan6 seng4 jat6 maai5 lai4 dong3 ling4 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我很喜欢吃炒米饼，小时候常常买来当零食。
examples.english_sentence: I really like eating puffed rice cakes; when I was a kid I used to buy them as snacks all the time.

mandarin_meaning: 炒米粉
english_meaning: stir-fried rice vermicelli / stir-fried rice noodles
explanation_mandarin: 指以米粉或粉絲等為主料，與蔬菜、肉類或海鮮一起快炒而成的一道菜。亦可作動詞，表示把米粉炒熟。
explanation_english: Refers to a dish of rice vermicelli (or similar thin noodles) quickly stir-fried with vegetables, meat, or seafood. Can also be used as a verb meaning to stir-fry rice vermicelli.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間茶餐廳嘅炒粉好好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1 ge3 caau2 fan2 hou2 hou2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間茶餐廳的炒米粉很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: The stir-fried rice vermicelli at this cha chaan teng is very tasty.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）被解雇／把人解雇（相當於「炒魷魚」的強調說法）
english_meaning: An emphatic Cantonese slang for being fired or firing someone (equivalent to 'to be sacked' / 'to sack someone').
explanation_mandarin: 「炒老世魷魚」是粵語口語俚語，為「炒魷魚」的強調或粗俗變體，用來表示把人解雇或被解雇。常見於香港口語中，可用被動結構如「畀人炒老世魷魚」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang term, an emphatic (and somewhat coarse or jocular) variant of "炒魷魚" (caau2 jau4 jyu4), used to mean "to fire someone" or "to be fired." Common in Hong Kong spoken Cantonese; often appears in passive constructions (e.g., "be sacked").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你再咁懶，可能會畀人炒老世魷魚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 zoi3 gam2 laan5, ho2 nang4 wui5 bei2 jan4 caau2 lou5 sai3 jau4 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你再這麼懶，可能會被人炒魷魚（被解雇）。
examples.english_sentence: If you stay this lazy, you might get fired.

mandarin_meaning: 把老闆解雇/罷免（俚語）
english_meaning: to sack/fire the boss (slang) — to remove or dismiss the boss
explanation_mandarin: 「炒魷魚」是香港粵語俚語，意指解雇或被解雇。將「老闆」放入，即「炒老板魷魚」，表示把老闆解雇、罷免或集體趕走老闆，常用於玩笑、群眾抗議或董事會罷免等情境。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese, "炒魷魚" is a slang term meaning to be fired or to sack someone. "炒老板魷魚" specifically means to sack or remove the boss — to dismiss the boss (used jokingly, in contexts of employee revolt, or formal removal by a board).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果啲員工聯手，真係可以炒老板魷魚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 di1 jyun4 gung1 lyun4 sau2, zan1 hai6 ho2 ji5 caau2 lou5 baan2 jau4 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果員工聯手，真的可以把老闆炒掉。
examples.english_sentence: If the employees unite, they could really sack the boss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 董事會決定炒老板魷魚，因為佢涉嫌貪污。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dong2 si6 wui6 kyut3 ding6 caau2 lou5 baan2 jau4 jyu4, jan1 wai6 keoi5 sip3 him2 taam1 wu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 董事會決定把老闆炒掉，因為他涉嫌貪污。
examples.english_sentence: The board decided to fire the boss because he was suspected of embezzlement.

mandarin_meaning: 把老闆開除；解雇老闆（幽默或諷刺用法）
english_meaning: to sack/fire the boss (humorous or sarcastic usage)
explanation_mandarin: 「炒魷魚」在廣東話中是被解雇的俚語；「炒老細魷魚」是把「老細」（老闆）作為被解雇的對象，常用作玩笑、諷刺或在勞資衝突、政治言論中表達要把老闆罷免或開除的意思。
explanation_english: Derived from the Cantonese slang "炒魷魚" (to be fired), "炒老細魷魚" literally means "to fry the boss squid" and is used to mean "to sack/fire the boss." It is usually humorous, sarcastic, or used in protest or satirical contexts rather than a literal employment-action term.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲員工話要炒老細魷魚，大家不過係講笑啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 jyun4 gung1 waa6 jiu3 caau2 lou5 sai3 jau4 jyu4, daai6 gaa1 bat1 gwo3 hai6 gong2 siu3 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 員工說要把老闆炒魷魚，大家只是在開玩笑罷了。
examples.english_sentence: The employees said they'd sack the boss, but everyone was just joking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋冇權炒老細魷魚，淨係可以辭職或者投訴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 mou5 kyun4 caau2 lou5 sai3 jau4 jyu4, zing6 hai6 ho2 ji5 ci4 zik1 waak6 ze2 tau4 sou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們沒有權力把老闆解雇，只能辭職或提出投訴。
examples.english_sentence: We don't have the power to sack the boss; we can only resign or file a complaint.

mandarin_meaning: 把老闆炒魷魚／解雇、罷免老闆（俚語，用來表示將老闆撤職）
english_meaning: to sack/fire the boss; to oust the boss (colloquial, humorous)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面是「把老闆炒魷魚」，用來幽默或諷刺地表示把老闆解雇或罷免，常指員工聯合要求或實際將老闆撤職。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning "to fry the boss squid." It humorously or ironically means to dismiss or oust the boss, often implying collective action by employees.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果老闆成日欺負員工，員工可能會諗住炒老闆魷魚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 lou5 baan2 seng4 jat6 hei1 fu6 jyun4 gung1, jyun4 gung1 ho2 nang4 wui5 lam2 zyu6 caau2 lou5 baan2 jau4 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果老闆經常欺負員工，員工可能會想著把老闆炒魷魚。
examples.english_sentence: If the boss keeps bullying staff, the employees might think about sacking the boss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 網上有條片講緊一班員工合力炒老闆魷魚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mong5 soeng6 jau5 tiu4 pin3 gong2 gan2 jat1 baan1 jyun4 gung1 hap6 lik6 caau2 lou5 baan2 jau4 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 網上有個影片在說一群員工聯手把老闆炒魷魚。
examples.english_sentence: There’s a video online about a group of employees teaming up to oust their boss.

mandarin_meaning: 炒股：投机性买卖股票（尤指短期买卖股票以获取利润）
english_meaning: to speculate in stocks; to trade stocks (especially short-term/speculative trading)
explanation_mandarin: 指以買賣股票為主要盈利方式，通常帶有短期投機成分，追求短期價差或快速獲利。
explanation_english: Refers to buying and selling stocks to make a profit, often involving short-term speculative trading to capture price movements.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺網上炒股，蝕咗好多錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai6 mong5 soeng6 caau2 gu2, sik1 zo2 hou2 do1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常在网上炒股，亏了很多钱。
examples.english_sentence: He often trades stocks online and has lost a lot of money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好隨便炒股，先學好基本分析同風險管理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 ceoi4 bin6 caau2 gu2, sin1 hok6 hou2 gei1 bun2 fan1 sik1 tung4 fung1 him2 gun2 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要随便炒股，先学好基本分析和风险管理。
examples.english_sentence: Don't casually speculate in stocks; first learn basic analysis and risk management.

mandarin_meaning: 炒股票 (chǎo gǔpiào)：投機性買賣股票，透過短期買入賣出以謀取差價利潤
english_meaning: to speculate in stocks; to trade stocks (typically short-term/speculatively) to make a profit
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指以短期買賣股票、利用價格波動賺取差價，通常帶有投機性並伴隨較高風險。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression meaning to buy and sell stocks with the aim of profiting from short-term price movements; implies speculative trading with relatively high risk.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日炒股票，希望快啲賺大錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 caau2 gu2 piu3, hei1 mong6 faai3 di1 zaan6 daai6 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常炒股票，希望快點賺大錢。
examples.english_sentence: He often speculates in stocks, hoping to make a quick fortune.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔建議你亂咁炒股票，風險好高。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 gin3 ji3 nei5 lyun6 gam2 caau2 gu2 piu3, fung1 him2 hou2 gou1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不建議你這樣亂炒股票，風險很高。
examples.english_sentence: I don't recommend recklessly speculating in stocks; the risks are very high.

mandarin_meaning: 炒芥蓝（chǎo jiè lán）
english_meaning: stir-fried gai lan (Chinese broccoli); a common Cantonese vegetable dish
explanation_mandarin: 指一道以芥蘭為主要材料，通常用蒜蓉或蠔油快炒的粵式蔬菜菜餚。既可以指菜名，也可指烹飪這道菜的動作。
explanation_english: Refers to a Cantonese dish of gai lan (Chinese broccoli) typically stir-fried quickly with garlic and often seasoned with oyster sauce. Can denote the dish itself or the action of stir-frying gai lan.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚食咩？去酒樓叫碟炒芥蘭啦，簡單又夠開胃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 sik6 me1? heoi3 zau2 lau4 giu3 dip6 caau2 gaai3 laan4 laa1, gaan2 daan1 jau6 gau3 hoi1 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚吃什麼？去酒樓點一盤炒芥藍吧，簡單又開胃。
examples.english_sentence: What shall we eat tonight? Let's go to the restaurant and order a plate of stir-fried gai lan — simple and appetizing.

mandarin_meaning: 炒蛋 / 炒鸡蛋
english_meaning: scrambled eggs
explanation_mandarin: 指將雞蛋打散後用油或奶等翻炒至熟的一道簡單菜餚，口感可軟滑或乾爽，亦常作早餐或配菜。
explanation_english: A dish made by beating eggs and frying them (often with butter, oil or milk) until cooked; texture can be soft and creamy or drier. Commonly eaten for breakfast or as a side.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 早餐我鍾意食炒蛋同多士。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou2 caan1 ngo5 zung1 ji3 sik6 caau2 daan6 tung4 do1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 早餐我喜欢吃炒蛋和吐司。
examples.english_sentence: I like to eat scrambled eggs and toast for breakfast.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲炒蛋做得好滑，好好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 caau2 daan6 zou6 dak1 hou2 waat6, hou2 hou2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的炒蛋做得很滑，很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: His scrambled eggs are very smooth and tasty.

mandarin_meaning: 渲染、炒作並挑剔拆解；煽動事端後逐一批評或挑毛病
english_meaning: To hype up or stir up something and then pick it apart; to create controversy or trouble and subsequently nitpick or criticize it
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，指有人刻意製造或渲染事端、炒作話題，然後對事件或人物逐一挑剔批評，造成爭議或煩擾。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning to deliberately stir up or hype an issue and then pick it apart — creating controversy and then nitpicking or criticizing the people/things involved.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再炒蝦拆蟹啦，搞到大家唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi3 caau2 haa1 caak3 haai5 laa1, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再製造事端並挑剔拆解了，弄得大家不開心。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep stirring up trouble and picking it apart; it's making everyone unhappy.

mandarin_meaning: 哄抬價格／抬高價格
english_meaning: to jack up prices; to speculate or gouge by inflating prices
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，指有人透過囤積或炒作等手段，故意抬高商品或服務的價格，帶有哄抬物價或投機牟利的意味。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang meaning to deliberately raise the price of goods or services by speculation, hoarding, or hype — essentially price-gouging or jacketing up prices for profit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲人為咗賺快錢成日炒貴刁，結果越炒越貴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 jan4 wai6 zo2 zaan6 faai3 cin2 sing4 jat6 caau2 gwai3 diu1, git3 gwo2 jyut6 caau2 jyut6 gwai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有人為了賺快錢經常哄抬價格，結果越炒越貴。
examples.english_sentence: People, trying to make quick money, often jack up prices — the more they hype it, the more expensive it becomes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 疫情期間有人炒貴刁，口罩賣到幾十蚊一個。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jik6 cing4 kei4 gaan1 jan4 jau5 caau2 gwai3 diu1, hau2 ziu3 maai6 dou3 gei2 sap6 man1 jat1 go3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 疫情期間有人哄抬價格，口罩賣到幾十塊錢一個。
examples.english_sentence: During the pandemic some people gouged prices, selling masks for dozens of dollars each.

mandarin_meaning: 炒卖；投机买卖（以短期买入卖出牟利）
english_meaning: to speculate; to buy and resell for short-term profit (speculative trading)
explanation_mandarin: 指以低買高賣或頻繁買賣以獲取短期利潤，常用於樓市、股票或商品等場合。
explanation_english: Refers to buying and selling (often repeatedly) to obtain short-term profit; commonly used for property, stocks, or goods speculation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家啲人成日喺樓市炒賣，搞到樓價好貴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 di1 jan4 sing4 jat6 hai2 lau4 si5 caau2 maai6, gaau2 dou3 lau4 gaa3 hou2 gwai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在的人经常在楼市炒卖，搞得房价很贵。
examples.english_sentence: Nowadays people often speculate in the property market, which has driven housing prices up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲投資者喺短期內炒賣股票，導致股價波動好大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 tau4 zi1 ze2 hai2 dyun2 kei4 noi6 caau2 maai6 gu2 piu3, dou6 zi3 gu2 gaa3 bo1 dung6 hou2 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一些投资者在短期内炒卖股票，导致股价波动很大。
examples.english_sentence: Some investors speculate in stocks over the short term, causing large price fluctuations.

mandarin_meaning: （1）翻炒；（2）炒作、煽动、炒高（价格、气氛、话题等）
english_meaning: 1) to stir-fry; 2) to hype up, stir up, inflate (a price, atmosphere, or topic)
explanation_mandarin: 「炒起」在廣東話有兩個常見用法：一是字面上的烹飪動作，指把材料翻炒；二是比喻用法，指炒作或煽動某種情緒、話題或抬高價格（例如炒起股價、炒起氣氛）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "炒起" has two common uses: literally to stir-fry ingredients; and metaphorically to hype up, stir up, or inflate something (e.g., driving up prices, whipping up an atmosphere, creating buzz).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰班人淨係識得炒起氣氛，無實際幫到手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 baan1 jan4 zing6 hai6 sik1 dak1 caau2 hei2 hei3 fan1, mou5 sat6 zai3 bong1 dou3 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些人只会炒热气氛，没实际帮忙。
examples.english_sentence: Those people only know how to hype up the atmosphere; they don't actually help.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個股畀佢哋炒起，股價一路上升。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 gu2 bei2 keoi5 dei6 caau2 hei2, gu2 gaa3 jat1 lou6 soeng5 sing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那只股票被他们炒高，股价一路上升。
examples.english_sentence: The stock was driven up by them; the price kept rising.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你可唔可以幫我炒起呢碟菜？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 caau2 hei2 ni1 dip6 coi3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你可以帮我把这盘菜炒一下吗？
examples.english_sentence: Could you stir-fry this dish for me?

mandarin_meaning: 撞車；出事；（俚語）失敗、出錯
english_meaning: to crash (a car); to get into a car accident; (slang) to have something go disastrously wrong, to fail spectacularly
explanation_mandarin: 「炒車」字面上指汽車相撞、發生車禍；在香港粵語口語中亦常作比喻，表示某件事嚴重出錯、失敗或計劃崩潰。
explanation_english: Literally means to have a car crash. In Hong Kong Cantonese it is also used figuratively to describe something going badly wrong, failing spectacularly, or collapsing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺高速公路上炒車，幸好冇人受傷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Keoi5 hai2 gou1cuk1 gung1lou6 soeng6 caau2 ce1, hang6hou2 mou5 jan4 sau6 soeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在高速公路上發生車禍，幸好沒有人受傷。
examples.english_sentence: He crashed on the highway; fortunately no one was injured.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次投資真係炒車晒，我哋蝕咗好多錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Gam1 ci3 tau4zi1 zan1hai6 caau2 ce1 saai3, ngo5dei6 sek3 zo2 hou2 do1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次投資真是失敗了，我們虧了很多錢。
examples.english_sentence: This investment really tanked; we lost a lot of money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢準備唔夠，簡報講到一半就炒車，連老闆都嬲親。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Keoi5 zeon2bei6 m4 gau3, gaan2bou3 gong2 dou3 jat1 bun3 zau6 caau2 ce1, lin4 lou5baan2 dou1 nau5 can1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他準備不足，簡報進行到一半就崩潰了，連老闆都生氣了。
examples.english_sentence: He wasn't prepared; the presentation fell apart halfway and even the boss got angry.

mandarin_meaning: 惹上麻煩；把事情弄糟；闖禍
english_meaning: to mess up; to cause/get into trouble; to make a mess of things
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面是「炒鍋」，引申為把事情弄得很糟、惹出麻煩或闖禍（可指自己出事或把別人捲入麻煩）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase literally meaning "to stir the wok." It is used to say someone has messed things up, caused trouble, or gotten into trouble (can imply causing problems for oneself or involving others).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再炒鑊啦，大家都唔想惹麻煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 caau2 wok6 laa1, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 soeng2 je5 maa4 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再惹事了，大家都不想招惹麻煩。
examples.english_sentence: Don't cause more trouble — nobody wants to get involved in problems.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事係佢炒鑊，唔可以咁樣推卸責任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 hai6 keoi5 caau2 wok6, m4 ho2 ji5 gam2 joeng6 teoi1 se6 zaak3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件事是他惹出來的，不能這樣推卸責任。
examples.english_sentence: He/she is the one who caused this problem; you can't shirk responsibility like that.

mandarin_meaning: 挑起事端；煽動是非
english_meaning: to stir up trouble; to deliberately create or amplify a fuss
explanation_mandarin: 俚語，形容人喜歡挑起糾紛或把小事弄大，故意煽動或誇大事端。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression describing someone who likes to stir up trouble or deliberately exaggerate small matters to create a fuss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日鍾意炒鑊勁，啲小事都要搞到好大件事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zung1 ji3 caau2 wok6 ging6, di1 siu2 si6 dou1 jiu3 gaau2 dou3 hou2 daai6 gin6 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常喜歡挑起事端，把小事情弄得很嚴重。
examples.english_sentence: He/She is always stirring up trouble, turning small matters into big issues.

mandarin_meaning: 炒作、製造話題或熱度（如為推廣或吸引注意而刻意宣傳）
english_meaning: to create hype or buzz; to artificially promote or stir up attention for something
explanation_mandarin: 指刻意製造話題或熱度以吸引公眾注意或推廣某人某事，常帶有誇大或炒作的意味，常用於媒體、宣傳或公關情境。
explanation_english: Refers to deliberately generating buzz or publicity to attract public attention or promote someone/something; often implies artificial promotion or exaggeration, commonly used in media, PR, or marketing contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 間公司為咗銷量，不斷炒風宣傳新產品。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaan1 gung1 si1 wai6 zo2 siu1 loeng6, bat1 dyun6 caau2 fung1 syun1 cyun4 san1 caan2 ban2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司為了銷量，不斷炒作宣傳新產品。
examples.english_sentence: The company keeps hyping the new product to boost sales.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲新聞媒體有時會炒風嚟吸引讀者。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 san1 man4 mui4 tai2 jau5 si4 wui5 caau2 fung1 lai4 kap1 jan5 duk6 ze2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一些新聞媒體有時會炒作來吸引讀者。
examples.english_sentence: Some news media sometimes create hype to attract readers.

mandarin_meaning: 放鴿子（爽約、不赴約）
english_meaning: to stand someone up; to bail on plans; to not show up for an appointment
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，指在約定的時間和地點沒有出現，放別人鴿子或臨時爽約。
explanation_english: A slang term meaning to fail to show up at an arranged meeting or appointment — to stand someone up or flake on plans.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢約咗我喺咖啡店見面，結果佢炒飛機，冇嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 joek3 zo2 ngo5 hai2 gaa3 fe1 dim3 gin3 min6, git3 gwo2 keoi5 caau2 fei1 gei1, mou5 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他約我在咖啡店見面，結果他放我鴿子，沒來。
examples.english_sentence: He asked me to meet at a café, but he stood me up and didn't show.

mandarin_meaning: 炒饭
english_meaning: fried rice
explanation_mandarin: 一种把熟米饭与鸡蛋、蔬菜、肉类等配料在锅中翻炒而成的米饭菜肴，常见的家常或餐厅菜式。
explanation_english: A rice dish made by stir-frying cooked rice with ingredients such as eggs, vegetables, and meat; a common home-style or restaurant dish.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚想食炒飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 soeng2 sik6 caau2 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚想吃炒饭。
examples.english_sentence: I want to eat fried rice tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢整嘅蛋炒飯好入味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing2 ge3 daan6 caau2 faan6 hou2 jap6 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做的蛋炒饭很入味。
examples.english_sentence: The egg fried rice he made is very flavorful.

mandarin_meaning: 炒菜 / 做菜
english_meaning: to cook dishes (usually stir-fry); to prepare a meal
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语，指在家或厨房里炒菜、准备菜肴。『餸』指配饭的菜肴，常用于香港粤语。
explanation_english: A Cantonese verb phrase meaning to cook or prepare dishes for a meal (often by stir-frying). '餸' refers to the dishes served with rice; commonly used in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚唔好出街，我喺屋企炒餸啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 m4 hou2 ceot1 gaai1, ngo5 hai2 uk1 kei5 caau2 sung3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚不要出去，我在家做菜吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's not eat out tonight — I'll cook at home.

mandarin_meaning: 被解雇；炒魷魚（解雇、开除）
english_meaning: to be fired; to sack someone (colloquial, short for '炒魷魚')
explanation_mandarin: 香港口語俚語，為“炒魷魚”的簡稱，意指被公司或老闆解雇、開除某人。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong colloquial slang term, short for '炒魷魚', meaning to be fired or to sack someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我上個月畀公司炒魷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng6 go3 jyut6 bei2 gung1 si1 caau2 jau4
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我上个月被公司解雇。
examples.english_sentence: I was fired by the company last month.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆話如果你再遲到就炒魷你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 waa6 jyu4 gwo2 nei5 zoi3 ci4 dou3 zau6 caau2 jau4 nei5
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板说如果你再迟到就把你炒了。
examples.english_sentence: The boss said if you're late again, he'll fire you.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）被解雇 / 炒鱿鱼
english_meaning: to be fired; to sack someone (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是「炒魷魚」，在廣東話口語中是俚語，表示被公司或上司解雇或開除。
explanation_english: Literally 'to fry squid', this Cantonese slang phrase means to be fired or to sack someone from a job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢畀公司炒魷魚喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 gung1 si1 chaau2 jau4 jyu4 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被公司炒鱿鱼了。
examples.english_sentence: He was fired by the company.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你做唔好工作就小心會畀老闆炒魷魚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 zou6 m4 hou2 gung1 zok3 zau6 siu2 sam1 wui5 bei2 lou5 baan2 chaau2 jau4 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果工作做不好就小心會被老板炒鱿鱼。
examples.english_sentence: If you don't do your job well, be careful—you might get fired by the boss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司決定炒魷魚三個員工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 kyut3 ding6 chaau2 jau4 jyu4 saam1 go3 jyun4 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司決定解雇三名員工。
examples.english_sentence: The company decided to dismiss three employees.

mandarin_meaning: 炒面（chǎomiàn）
english_meaning: stir-fried noodles; chow mein
explanation_mandarin: 指用油將麵條與配料（如蔬菜、肉類、醬料）一起翻炒而成的菜餚，在香港常見的做法有乾炒或湯炒等不同風格。
explanation_english: Refers to noodles stir-fried with ingredients (such as vegetables, meat, and sauces). Common in Hong Kong and elsewhere, it can be served dry or with sauce; also known as chow mein.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間茶餐廳嘅炒麪真係好好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1 ge3 caau2 min6 zan1 hai6 hou2 hou2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家茶餐厅的炒面真的很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: The fried noodles at this cha chaan teng are really delicious.

mandarin_meaning: 炒面 / 炒麵
english_meaning: stir-fried noodles / fried noodles
explanation_mandarin: 炒麵是一種將麵條與蔬菜、肉類或海鮮等配料在鍋中翻炒而成的菜餚。根據地區與做法不同，調味與配料會有所差異，是華人飲食中常見的主食或快餐選擇。
explanation_english: Stir-fried noodles: a dish made by frying noodles with vegetables, meat, or seafood in a wok or pan. Seasoning and ingredients vary by region and recipe. It is a common main dish or quick meal in Chinese cuisines.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我想食炒麵，茶餐廳嗰間有好出名嘅乾炒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 soeng2 sik6 caau2 min6, caa4 caan1 teng1 go2 gaan1 jau5 hou2 ceot1 ming4 ge3 gon1 caau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我想吃炒面，那間茶餐厅的乾炒很有名。
examples.english_sentence: I want to eat fried noodles tonight; that cha chaan teng's dry-fried noodles are famous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你試過佢哋嘅海鮮炒麵未？有好多蝦同魷魚，好好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 si3 gwo3 keoi5 dei6 ge3 hoi2 sin1 caau2 min6 mei6? jau5 hou2 do1 haa1 tung4 jau4 jyu4, hou2 hou2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你試過他們的海鮮炒面嗎？有很多蝦和魷魚，非常好吃。
examples.english_sentence: Have you tried their seafood fried noodles? It has lots of shrimp and squid — very tasty.

mandarin_meaning: 炒面
english_meaning: fried noodles; chow mein
explanation_mandarin: 以油和高溫快炒的麵食，通常會加入蔬菜、肉類或調味料，是中式餐館與街頭小吃常見菜肴。
explanation_english: A noodle dish stir-fried in oil over high heat, often with vegetables, meat, and seasonings; commonly known as chow mein or fried noodles.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚想食炒麵。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 soeng2 sik6 caau2 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚想吃炒面。
examples.english_sentence: I want to eat fried noodles tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 倒卖（门票或热门商品），做黄牛
english_meaning: to scalp; to resell tickets or in-demand goods at inflated prices (engage in touting)
explanation_mandarin: 指以高价倒卖演唱会门票或其他熱門商品，以牟取差价的行为，即黄牛的行为。
explanation_english: To engage in scalping — reselling tickets or popular goods at inflated prices to make a profit (the activity of touts/scalpers).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次演唱會嘅門票畀人炒黃牛，價錢貴到不得了。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 jin2 coeng3 wui6 ge3 mun4 piu3 bei2 jan4 caau2 wong4 ngau4, gaa3 cin2 gwai3 dou3 bat1 dak1 liu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次演唱会的门票被黄牛倒卖，价格贵得离谱。
examples.english_sentence: Tickets for this concert were scalped by touts; the prices are ridiculously high.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）抹黑、炒作負面消息
english_meaning: to smear (someone); to hype up negative information about someone
explanation_mandarin: 指透過媒體、社交平台或其他渠道，翻出、放大或刻意製造他人過去的負面事件或醜聞，以損害對方名譽或形象。
explanation_english: A colloquial slang phrase meaning to dig up or amplify someone's past negative incidents (often via media or social platforms) in order to smear them and damage their reputation or image.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲記者成日鍾意炒黑底，將佢以前啲醜聞翻出嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 gei3 ze2 sing4 jat6 zung1 ji3 caau2 hak1 dai2, zoeng1 keoi5 ji5 cin4 di1 cau2 man4 faan1 ceot1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些記者總愛抹黑，挖出他以前的醜聞來。
examples.english_sentence: The reporters always love to smear him, digging up his past scandals.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政治人物好驚畀對手炒黑底，所以處理過去嘅事特別小心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 zi6 jan4 mat6 hou2 geng1 paa3 bei2 deoi3 sau2 caau2 hak1 dai2, so2 ji5 cyu5 lei5 gwo3 heoi3 ge3 si6 dak6 bit6 siu2 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政治人物很害怕被對手抹黑，所以處理過去的事特別小心。
examples.english_sentence: Politicians are afraid of being smeared by opponents, so they handle past matters especially carefully.

mandarin_meaning: 炔（化学名）——指含碳碳三键的烃类，或作为有机化学命名后缀（-yne）
english_meaning: Alkyne (chemical term) — a hydrocarbon with a carbon–carbon triple bond; also the suffix '-yne' in organic nomenclature
explanation_mandarin: 化学术语，指含有碳—碳三键的一类烃（如乙炔），在命名中也作为后缀表示“-yne”。
explanation_english: A chemistry term referring to hydrocarbons that contain a carbon–carbon triple bond (e.g., acetylene); used as the suffix '-yne' in organic compound names.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 乙炔係一種常用嘅燃料，用嚟切割金屬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jat6 kyut3 hai6 jat1 zung2 soeng4 jung6 ge3 jin4 liu6, jung6 lai4 cit3 got3 gam1 suk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 乙炔是一种常用的燃料，用来切割金属。
examples.english_sentence: Acetylene is a commonly used fuel, used to cut metal.

mandarin_meaning: 炕（kàng）——一种用砖或土筑成、内部可通烟道以取暖的床或床台，北方常见。
english_meaning: Kang — a heated brick or earthen bed (common in northern China) used for sleeping and warming.
explanation_mandarin: 指北方民居常见的炕，即用砖、土等筑成并能通烟道以供取暖的床或床台，冬季用于睡觉取暖。
explanation_english: Refers to the kang — a traditional northern-Chinese heated bed or platform made of brick or packed earth with flues for heating; used for sleeping and keeping warm in winter.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 冬天我哋北方嘅屋企通常會有炕，瞓喺炕上好暖。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dung1 tin1 ngo5 dei6 bak1 fong1 ge3 uk1 kei2 tung1 soeng4 wui5 jau5 kong3, fan3 hai2 kong3 soeng6 hou2 nyun5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 冬天我们北方的房子通常有炕，睡在炕上很暖和。
examples.english_sentence: In winter, northern homes usually have a kang; sleeping on the kang is very warm.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我屋企冇炕，所以冬天要開暖爐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 uk1 kei2 mou5 kong3, so2 ji5 dung1 tin1 jiu3 hoi1 nyun5 lou4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我家没有炕，所以冬天要开暖炉。
examples.english_sentence: My home doesn't have a kang, so we have to use a heater in winter.

mandarin_meaning: 炕几（方言/地區用語），指放在炕上或靠近炕邊的矮小桌子或台面。
english_meaning: A small low table or bench placed on or beside a kang (a heated bed/platform) — a regional/dialect household item.
explanation_mandarin: “炕几”屬於方言詞，多見於北方或部分南方方言語境，字面上由“炕”（供人坐臥的台面或暖炕）與“几”（小桌）組成，指放在炕上或靠炕邊的矮桌、矮台，常用來擺放茶具、碗盤或日用品。
explanation_english: “炕几” is a regional/dialectal term literally combining 'kang' (a raised/ heated platform for sitting or sleeping) and 'ji' (a small table). It refers to a low table or bench placed on or next to a kang, typically used to hold tea, dishes, or everyday items.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽喺炕几上擺咗杯茶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 hai2 hong3 gei1 soeng6 baai2 zo2 bui1 caa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽在炕几上擺了杯茶。
examples.english_sentence: Mom placed a cup of tea on the kang-table.

mandarin_meaning: 炕（炕台、暖炕），一种带有加热功能的砖台床，北方民居用来取暖和睡觉的床
english_meaning: kang bed (heated brick/platform bed common in northern China used for heating and sleeping)
explanation_mandarin: 炕床指北方傳統建築裡的一種用磚或土搭成的高台床，內部或下方有火道或煙道可加熱，用於取暖和睡覺，常見於中國北方農村和一些老式民居中。
explanation_english: A traditional northern Chinese heated bed — a raised brick or earthen platform (kang) with internal flues or channels for heating. Used for warmth and sleeping, commonly found in rural northern China and older dwellings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我細個喺北方屋企係炕床上面瞓大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 hai2 bak1 fong1 uk1 kei2 hai6 kong3 cong4 soeng6 min6 fan3 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我小时候在北方家里在炕床上长大。
examples.english_sentence: I grew up sleeping on a kang bed at my home in the north.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 北方嘅炕床用嚟取暖同埋瞓覺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bak1 fong1 ge3 kong3 cong4 jung6 lai4 ceoi2 nyun5 tung4 maai4 fan3 gok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 北方的炕用来取暖和睡觉。
examples.english_sentence: Kang beds in northern China are used for heating and sleeping.

mandarin_meaning: 炕的下面；床炕下方的空間（常用於儲物或躲藏）
english_meaning: the space under a kang (heated brick bed); the area beneath a bed often used for storage or hiding
explanation_mandarin: 指北方房屋中有暖炕時，炕的下方空間。該處常用來收納被褥、衣物或作為躲藏處，亦可泛指床下空間。
explanation_english: Refers to the space beneath a kang (a heated bed common in northern China). This area is often used for storing quilts, clothes, or as a hiding place; it can also be used more generally to mean 'under the bed.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿婆將冬天嘅衫收喺炕底。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 po4 zoeng1 dung1 tin1 ge3 saam1 sau1 hai2 kong3 dai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 奶奶把冬天的衣服收在炕底。
examples.english_sentence: Grandma put the winter clothes away under the kang.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路仔喺炕底躲貓貓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 zai2 hai2 kong3 dai2 do2 maau1 maau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 孩子躲在炕底玩捉迷藏。
examples.english_sentence: The child hid under the kang to play hide-and-seek.

mandarin_meaning: 炕枕（放在炕上使用的枕头）
english_meaning: kang pillow; a pillow used on a kang (heated brick bed/platform)
explanation_mandarin: 指放在炕（北方傳統的帶加熱的床臺）上用來枕頭或靠背的小枕頭，常見於北方農家或傳統民居。
explanation_english: Refers to a pillow placed on a kang (a traditional heated brick bed/platform common in northern China), used for resting the head or as a backrest; typical in traditional rural homes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢屋企炕上擺住幾個炕枕，好有傳統風味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 uk1 kei5 hong3 soeng6 baai2 zyu6 gei2 go3 hong3 zam2, hou2 jau5 cyun4 tung2 fung1 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他家里在炕上放了幾個炕枕，很有傳統風味。
examples.english_sentence: They had several kang pillows on the kang in their home; it looked very traditional.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見詞彙；可能是方言、口語或打字錯誤，沒有被廣泛記錄或達成共識的義項。
english_meaning: Obscure/rare term; possibly a regional dialect, colloquial slang, or a typographical error with no widely agreed meaning.
explanation_mandarin: 「炕沙」在現有粵語詞典與語料中很少見，缺乏可靠定義。它可能是地區方言詞、口語俚語或輸入錯誤。遇到此詞時建議向說話者求證具體含義與用法。
explanation_english: The term '炕沙' is scarcely attested in current Cantonese references and lacks a reliable definition. It may be a regional dialect word, colloquial slang, or simply a typo. When encountering it, verify the meaning and usage with the speaker.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺街聽到有人講「炕沙」，但我唔知佢哋講緊咩意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gaai1 teng1 dou3 jau5 jan4 gong2 "kong3 saa1", daan6 ngo5 m4 zi1 keoi5 dei6 gong2 gan2 me1 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在街上聽到有人說「炕沙」，但我不知道他們在說什麼意思。
examples.english_sentence: I heard someone say '炕沙' on the street, but I don't know what they meant.

mandarin_meaning: 炖（燉）
english_meaning: to stew; to simmer
explanation_mandarin: 表示用小火和液體長時間煮，使食材變爛、入味。繁體常寫作「燉」。
explanation_english: To cook food slowly in liquid over low heat until tender and flavorful; commonly written as 燉 in traditional Chinese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽媽今晚炖咗隻雞，成屋都好香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 maa1 gam1 maan5 deon6 zo2 zek3 gai1, sing4 uk1 dou1 hou2 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈今晚炖了一只鸡，整个屋子都很香。
examples.english_sentence: Mom stewed a chicken tonight; the whole house smells delicious.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）指行動或反應遲緩、顯得老態龍鍾的老人；也可作帶貶義的稱呼，指遲鈍的人
english_meaning: colloquial/slang: an old geezer who is slow-moving or slow-witted; a derogatory term for someone sluggish or senile
explanation_mandarin: 「炖翁」字面上是「燉」加「翁」，口語用作俚語，多用來形容年紀大且行動或反應慢的人，有貶義，屬非正式用法。
explanation_english: Literally combines the characters for 'stew' and 'old man'; used colloquially to describe an elderly person (or anyone) who is slow in movement or thinking. It is informal and often derogatory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個炖翁成日喺度慢吞吞，做嘢好慢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 deon6 jung1 sing4 jat6 hai2 dou6 maan6 tan1 tan1, zou6 je5 hou2 maan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那個「炖翁」總是在那裡慢吞吞，做事很慢。
examples.english_sentence: That old geezer is always dawdling there and works very slowly.

mandarin_meaning: 烤、炙烤；也用于成语中比喻权势或名望很高（如“炙手可热”）
english_meaning: to roast or broil (with fire); figuratively, to be extremely popular or powerful (as in the idiom '炙手可热')
explanation_mandarin: 表示用火烤、烧食物，使表面焦香；在引申意义上，常见于成语中，形容人或事物權勢、名望極高，令人難以接近。
explanation_english: Refers to cooking by roasting or searing with fire, producing a charred, fragrant surface. Figuratively, it appears in idioms to describe someone or something very influential or popular.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 師傅用火炙牛肉，令表面焦香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si1 fu6 jung6 fo2 zik6 ngau4 juk6, ling6 biu2 min6 ziu1 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 师傅用火炙牛肉，让表面焦香。
examples.english_sentence: The chef seared the beef with fire, giving it a charred, fragrant surface.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家炙手可熱，成日都有傳媒追訪。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 zik6 sau2 ho2 jit6, sing4 jat6 dou1 jau5 cyun4 mui4 zeoi1 fong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在炙手可热，经常有媒体追访。
examples.english_sentence: He is now extremely popular/influential; the media frequently pursues him.

mandarin_meaning: 炙手可热 (zhì shǒu kě rè)：比喻名望或權勢極大，令人畏懼或極為搶手、熱門。
english_meaning: Red-hot; extremely popular or influential; so in-demand or powerful that figuratively one would be 'burned' by touching.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻名聲、權勢或人氣非常高，讓人畏懼或爭相追逐，常用來形容某人或某事物非常熱門或有影響力。
explanation_english: An idiom used to describe someone or something with great prestige, power, or popularity — so influential or sought-after that contact would be 'burning'; used adjectivally to mean 'very hot' or 'highly sought-after.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢位歌手而家炙手可熱，演唱會門票一開賣即刻賣晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 wai2 go1 sau2 ji4 gaa1 zek3 sau2 ho2 jit6, jin2 coeng3 wui6 mun4 piu3 jat1 hoi1 maai6 zik1 hak1 maai6 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这位歌手现在炙手可热，演唱会门票一开售就立刻售罄。
examples.english_sentence: This singer is currently red-hot; concert tickets sold out as soon as they went on sale.

mandarin_meaning: 炙火（明火、用于炙烤或灼烧的火焰；猛烈的热力）
english_meaning: open flame used for roasting or searing; intense, blazing heat
explanation_mandarin: 指用于炙烤、灼烧食物的明火或強烈的火焰，有時也用來形容猛烈的熱力或烤炙的過程。
explanation_english: Refers to an open flame used for roasting or searing food, or an intense blazing heat; can also describe the process of searing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 廚師用炙火燒住三文魚，表面好香脆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cyu4 si1 jung6 zek3 fo2 siu1 zyu6 saam1 man4 jyu4, biu2 min6 hou2 hoeng1 ceoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 厨师用炙火烧三文鱼，表面很香脆。
examples.english_sentence: The chef sears the salmon over an open flame; the surface is very fragrant and crispy.

mandarin_meaning: 炙烧 (zhìshāo)；用强烈热力把表面烧烤或烧焦
english_meaning: to sear / to torch / to scorch (typically by applying intense heat to the surface, often in cooking)
explanation_mandarin: 表示用強烈熱力燒烤或把表面迅速燒焦（常用於烹飪，如用噴火槍炙燒魚皮），也可泛指太陽或高溫灼熱物體。
explanation_english: To apply intense heat to something to sear or scorch its surface (commonly used in cooking, e.g., using a blowtorch on fish), or more generally to describe scorching by sun or high heat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 廚師用噴火槍炙燒三文魚腩，令表面微焦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceoi4 si1 jung6 pan3 fo2 coeng1 zaak6 siu1 saam1 man4 jyu4 naam5, ling6 biu2 min6 mei4 ziu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 厨师用喷火枪炙烤三文鱼腹，使表面微焦。
examples.english_sentence: The chef used a blowtorch to sear the salmon belly, giving the surface a slight char.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 炎陽炙燒大地，大家要記得多飲水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jim4 joeng4 zaak6 siu1 daai6 dei6, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 gei3 dak1 do1 jam2 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 炎阳炙烤着大地，大家要记得多喝水。
examples.english_sentence: The scorching sun is baking the earth; everyone should remember to drink more water.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見字，現代漢語中無固定或常用的詞義與讀音；多見於古籍或字書作為異體字或罕用字。
english_meaning: A rare/obsolete character with no fixed modern Mandarin reading or common meaning; mainly attested as a historical or variant character.
explanation_mandarin: 「炩」為罕用漢字，現代普通話和廣東話中均無普遍接受的讀音或詞義。它偶見於古籍或字典中，常被視為異體字或已廢用的字形。如無特定語境，不建議在現代書寫或會話中使用。
explanation_english: The character '炩' is a rare/archaic Chinese character without an established modern Mandarin or Cantonese pronunciation or common meaning. It appears occasionally in historical texts or dictionaries as a variant character. It is not used in everyday speech or writing in contemporary Chinese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字「炩」好罕見，平時唔會用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 '炩' hou2 hon2 gin3, ping4 si4 m4 wui5 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字“炩”很罕见，平时不会用。
examples.english_sentence: The character '炩' is very rare; it's not used in everyday language.

mandarin_meaning: 黏糊糊、黏稠（口語擬聲）
english_meaning: sticky, gooey (colloquial/onomatopoeic)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話的擬聲詞或口語用語，用來形容東西黏糊、黏在一起或潮濕黏膩的感覺，多用於日常口語描述衣物、食物或物件表面黏性。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial onomatopoeic term used to describe something that is sticky or gooey — things that cling, are tacky or wet and adhesive. Commonly used in everyday speech for clothing, food or surfaces that feel sticky.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 件衫整到炩擸擸，真係唔好著。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin6 saam1 zing2 dou3 gong2 laai1 laai1, zan1 hai6 m4 hou2 zoek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 衣服弄得黏糊糊，真的不適合穿。
examples.english_sentence: The shirt got all sticky and gooey — it's really not wearable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友玩完糖果，手指都炩擸擸，要洗手先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 waan2 jyun4 tong4 gwo2, sau2 zi2 dou1 gong2 laai1 laai1, jiu3 sai2 sau2 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友吃完糖果，手指都黏糊糊的，要先洗手。
examples.english_sentence: After kids eat sweets their fingers are all sticky; they need to wash their hands first.

jyutping: man4 min6 (likely a nonstandard / mistaken writing of 炆面)
mandarin_meaning: 焖面／炆面（慢火燜煮的麵條）
english_meaning: braised/simmered noodles (noodles cooked slowly in sauce or broth)
explanation_mandarin: 「炩面」這個寫法在書面上非常少見，通常是打字或筆誤。正確且常見的廣東話寫法為「炆面」（粵語讀作 man4 min6），指以慢火燜煮或燴煮的麵條，是一道常見的家常或茶餐廳菜式。
explanation_english: The form "炩面" is very uncommon and is usually a typo or nonstandard spelling. The usual Cantonese form is "炆面" (Jyutping: man4 min6), meaning braised or simmered noodles — noodles slowly cooked in a sauce or broth, a common home or diner dish in Cantonese-speaking areas.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚想食炩面，但其實應該寫做炆面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 soeng2 sik6 man4 min6, daan6 kei4 sat6 jing1 goi1 se2 zou6 man4 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚想吃炩面，但其实应该写作炆面。
examples.english_sentence: I want to eat "炩面" tonight, but it should actually be written as "炆面" (braised noodles).

mandarin_meaning: 炫（xuàn）：炫耀、显眼、光彩夺目
english_meaning: to show off; dazzling; eye-catching
explanation_mandarin: 表示夸示、卖弄或光彩夺目。可作动词（如“炫耀”）表示炫示、卖弄；亦可作形容词（如“炫目”）表示令人目眩、醒目。
explanation_english: Means to show off or to be dazzling/eye-catching. Used as a verb (to flaunt/show off) or as an adjective (dazzling). In Cantonese it's commonly used to mean displaying or flaunting something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺IG度炫新衫，真係好煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai6 ai1 gei1 dou6 hyun3 san1 saam1, zan1 hai6 hou2 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常在IG上炫耀新衣服，真让人讨厌。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps showing off his new clothes on IG — it's really annoying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 演唱會嘅燈光好炫目，幾刺激。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jin2 coeng3 wui2 ge3 dang1 gwong1 hou2 hyun3 muk6, gei2 cik1 gik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 演唱会的灯光很炫目，挺刺激的。
examples.english_sentence: The concert lights are dazzling; it's quite thrilling.

mandarin_meaning: 炫耀财富
english_meaning: to flaunt one's wealth; to show off riches
explanation_mandarin: 指有意展示或炫耀自己的财富、奢侈品或高消费生活方式，常带贬义或批评意味。
explanation_english: To deliberately display or flaunt one's wealth, luxury goods, or expensive lifestyle, often with a negative or critical connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺Instagram度炫富，晒啲名牌包同名車。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 Instagram dou6 hyun6 fu3, saai3 di1 ming4 paai4 baau1 tung4 ming4 ce1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是在Instagram上炫富，晒名牌包和名车。
examples.english_sentence: He is always flaunting his wealth on Instagram, showing off designer bags and luxury cars.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日炫富，會得罪朋友。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 hyun6 fu3, wui5 dak1 zeoi6 pang4 jau5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要总是炫富，会得罪朋友。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep flaunting your wealth; you'll offend your friends.

mandarin_meaning: 炫耀 (xuànyào)：夸示、显摆，卖弄自己的优点、财物或成就。
english_meaning: to show off; to flaunt; to boast
explanation_mandarin: 表示故意夸示自己的优点、财物或成就，以引起他人注意或羡慕，常带有贬义。
explanation_english: To deliberately display one's possessions, abilities, or achievements in order to attract attention or admiration; often has a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日炫耀佢啲名牌衫，人人都覺得煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hyun3 jiu6 keoi5 di1 ming4 paai4 saam1, jan4 jan4 dou1 gok3 dak1 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是在炫耀他的名牌衣服，大家都觉得烦。
examples.english_sentence: He's always showing off his designer clothes; everyone finds it annoying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好喺我面前炫耀你啲錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 hai2 ngo5 min6 cin4 hyun3 jiu6 nei5 di1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別在我面前炫耀你的錢。
examples.english_sentence: Don't flaunt your money in front of me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢冇必要成日喺社交媒體上炫耀自己啲成就。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mou5 bit1 jiu3 sing4 jat6 hai2 se5 gaau1 mui4 tai2 soeng6 hyun3 jiu6 zi6 gei2 di1 seng4 zau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他没必要总是在社交媒体上炫耀自己的成就。
examples.english_sentence: He doesn't need to constantly brag about his achievements on social media.

mandarin_meaning: 火炬；火把（常見於「火炬」、「火炬傳遞」等）
english_meaning: torch; flaming torch (often used in compounds like 'torch relay')
explanation_mandarin: 指用來照明或作為象徵的火把、火炬，常用於儀式或慶典（如火炬傳遞）。在漢語中多見於複合詞如「火炬」。
explanation_english: Refers to a torch — a flaming stick or symbolic light used for illumination or ceremonial purposes. Commonly appears in compounds such as 'fire torch' or 'torch relay'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢手上拿住一把火炬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sau2 soeng6 naa4 zyu6 jat1 baa2 fo2 geoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他手上拿着一把火炬。
examples.english_sentence: He is holding a torch in his hand.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 火炬傳遞好感人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fo2 geoi6 cyun4 dai6 hou2 gam2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 火炬传递很感人。
examples.english_sentence: The torch relay is very moving.

mandarin_meaning: 炭；指木炭或煤炭等碳質燃料
english_meaning: charcoal; coal (carbonaceous fuel)
explanation_mandarin: 炭通常指木炭或煤炭，是由有機物部分燃燒或熱解後形成的黑色固體，常用作燃料或工業原料，也用於燒烤等日常用途。
explanation_english: Charcoal (or coal): a black carbonaceous solid formed by the partial combustion or pyrolysis of organic matter, commonly used as fuel, industrial material, or for grilling.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋用炭嚟燒烤啲肉，味道好香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jung6 taan3 lai4 siu1 haau1 di1 juk6, mei6 dou6 hou2 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们用炭来烧烤肉，味道很香。
examples.english_sentence: We use charcoal to grill the meat; it tastes really good.

mandarin_meaning: 炭炉 (tàn lú)：用炭燃燒的爐子，用於取暖或燒烤。
english_meaning: charcoal brazier / charcoal stove — a stove that burns charcoal for heating or cooking.
explanation_mandarin: 指用來燃燒木炭的爐具，常用於取暖或燒烤，在一些地區的家庭或戶外活動中會見到。
explanation_english: A stove or brazier that burns charcoal; commonly used for heating or grilling, seen in homes or outdoor gatherings in some regions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 冬天屋企擺住炭爐，成間屋都幾暖和。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dung1 tin1 uk1 kei2 baai2 zyu6 taan3 lou4, sing4 gaan1 uk1 dou1 gei2 nyun5 wo4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 冬天家裡放著炭炉，整間房子都很暖和。
examples.english_sentence: In winter we put a charcoal brazier at home; the whole house is quite warm.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋喺屋企用炭爐燒嘢食，味道好香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 hai2 uk1 kei2 jung6 taan3 lou4 siu1 je5 sik6, mei6 dou6 hou2 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我們在家用炭炉燒東西吃，味道很香。
examples.english_sentence: Tonight we're using a charcoal brazier at home to grill food; it smells delicious.

mandarin_meaning: 炭笔（用於繪畫的炭製畫筆/炭條）
english_meaning: charcoal pencil / charcoal stick (drawing tool)
explanation_mandarin: 用壓縮或原炭製作的繪圖工具，常用於素描、速寫和表現陰影及質感。
explanation_english: A drawing tool made from charcoal (compressed or natural), commonly used for sketching, figure drawing, and creating tones and textures.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 美術課要我帶炭筆去上堂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mei5 seot6 fo3 jiu3 ngo5 daai3 taan3 bat1 heoi3 soeng5 tong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 美术课要我带炭笔去上课。
examples.english_sentence: The art class asked me to bring charcoal pencils to class.

mandarin_meaning: 炭精（多指炭精筆或木炭條，用於素描或繪畫的炭條／筆芯）
english_meaning: charcoal (drawing material); charcoal/graphite pencil or stick used for sketching
explanation_mandarin: 指用於繪畫或素描的炭條、炭精筆或類似的石墨筆芯，質地適合做陰影、速寫與厚重線條。
explanation_english: Refers to charcoal sticks or charcoal/graphite pencils/leads used for drawing and sketching; well suited for shading, quick sketches, and bold strokes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲炭精係用嚟畫陰影嘅，好方便。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 taan3 zing1 hai6 jung6 lai4 waa6 jam1 jing2 ge3, hou2 fong1 bin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這些炭精是用來畫陰影的，很方便。
examples.english_sentence: These charcoals are used to draw shadows; they're very convenient.

mandarin_meaning: 炮（pào）：可指火炮、鞭炮；也可作動詞，如炮製（捏造、加工）；在口語俚語中與「打炮」連用指性交。
english_meaning: pao/paau: cannon or firecracker; to roast/prepare/concoct; slang (in phrase 'daa2 paau3' / '打炮') meaning to have sex.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞 / 動詞（視語境而定）
partOfSpeech_english: noun / verb (depends on context); slang verb (sexual)
explanation_mandarin: 「炮」在廣東話可作名詞表示砲、大炮或鞭炮；亦常見於複合動詞如「炮製」（捏造、加工）。在俗語中，「打炮」為粗俗俚語，意指發生性行為，需注意語境與禮貌。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 「炮」 (paau3) can mean cannon or firecracker as a noun, or be part of verbs such as 炮製 (to concoct/fabricate). In colloquial slang, 打炮 (daa2 paau3) is a vulgar expression meaning to have sex. Be aware of register and context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋喺派對尾偷偷打炮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 hai2 paai3 deoi6 mei5 tau1 tau1 daa2 paau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们在派对结束时偷偷打炮（发生性关系）。
examples.english_sentence: They secretly had sex at the end of the party.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢炮製咗份假報告嚟欺騙公司。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 paau3 zai3 zo2 fan6 gaa2 bou3 gou3 lai4 hei1 pin3 gung1 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他炮製了一份假报告来欺骗公司。
examples.english_sentence: He fabricated a fake report to deceive the company.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 春節嗰陣大家齊放炮慶祝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceon1 zit3 go2 zan6 daai6 gaa1 cai4 fong3 paau3 hing3 zuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 春节的时候大家一起放炮庆祝。
examples.english_sentence: During Lunar New Year people set off firecrackers together to celebrate.

mandarin_meaning: 小鞭炮 / 小炮仗
english_meaning: small firecracker; small banger
explanation_mandarin: 「炮仔」在粵語中通常指小型鞭炮或炮仗，用於節慶或慶祝活動。注意：粵語中「打炮」是粗俗用語指性行為，但「炮仔」一般指字面上的小鞭炮，不等同於該粗俗用法。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "炮仔" usually refers to a small firecracker used in celebrations. Note: the verb "打炮" in Cantonese can be a vulgar slang for sexual intercourse, but "炮仔" typically means the literal small firecracker and is not the same as that slang.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 除夕夜我哋放炮仔慶祝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceoi4 zik6 je6 ngo5 dei6 fong3 paau3 zai2 hing3 zuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 除夕夜我們放小鞭炮慶祝。
examples.english_sentence: On New Year's Eve we set off small firecrackers to celebrate.

mandarin_meaning: 鞭炮；爆竹
english_meaning: firecrackers
explanation_mandarin: 指用於慶祝場合的鞭炮、爆竹。口語中也可引申為誇張、喧鬧或放空話、吹噓的行為（如「放炮仗」）。
explanation_english: Refers to firecrackers used in celebrations. Colloquially it can be extended to mean noisy or boastful behavior or empty talk (e.g., 'setting off firecrackers' figuratively).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新年嗰陣，我哋成街都放緊炮仗，好熱鬧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 go2 zan6, ngo5 dei6 seng4 gaai1 dou1 fong3 gan2 paau3 zoeng6, hou2 jit6 naau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 过年时，我们整条街都在放炮仗，很热闹。
examples.english_sentence: During the New Year, the whole street was setting off firecrackers — it was very lively.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日放炮仗，冇人信佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 fong3 paau3 zoeng6, mou5 jan4 seon3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常放炮仗，沒有人相信他。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps making empty boasts; no one believes him.

mandarin_meaning: 鞭炮的引线／导火线
english_meaning: the fuse of a firecracker; figuratively, the trigger (or fuse) that sets off trouble or a conflict
explanation_mandarin: 指用來點燃炮仗（鞭炮）的引線；在口語中也常被比喻為引發矛盾或事端的導火線。
explanation_english: Refers to the fuse used to light firecrackers. In colloquial usage it can be used metaphorically to mean the trigger or spark that sets off a dispute or incident.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 過年買咗啲炮仗，點炮仗引嗰陣要小心，唔好傷到人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gwo3 nin4 maai5 zo2 di1 paau3 zoeng6, dim2 paau3 zoeng6 jan5 go2 zan6 jiu3 siu2 sam1, m4 hou2 soeng1 dou3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 过年买了些鞭炮，点燃炮仗引的时候要小心，别伤到人。
examples.english_sentence: We bought some firecrackers for Lunar New Year; be careful when lighting the fuses so nobody gets hurt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講咗幾句惹火嘅說話，成為咗呢單爭拗嘅炮仗引。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 zo2 gei2 geoi3 je5 fo2 ge3 syut3 waa6, sing4 wai4 zo2 ni1 daan1 zang1 au2 ge3 paau3 zoeng6 jan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說了幾句激怒人的話，成了這場爭執的導火線。
examples.english_sentence: He said some provocative things that became the fuse for the argument.

mandarin_meaning: 炮仗花（pào zhàng huā）
english_meaning: firecracker flower (ornamental plant with tubular red/orange flowers)
explanation_mandarin: 一種常見的觀賞植物，花呈筒狀或串狀，鮮紅或橙紅色，形狀像傳統炮仗，常於園藝種植或節日時用作裝飾。
explanation_english: A common ornamental plant whose tubular or clustered red/orange flowers resemble firecrackers; often grown in gardens and used as festive decoration.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋陽台擺咗幾盆炮仗花，好有過節氣氛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 joeng4 toi4 baai2 zo2 gei2 pun4 pou3 zong6 faa1, hou2 jau5 gwo3 zit3 hei3 fan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在陽台擺了幾盆炮仗花，很有過節的氣氛。
examples.english_sentence: We put a few pots of firecracker flowers on the balcony — it gives a festive atmosphere.

mandarin_meaning: 脾气暴躁、容易发脾气（口语）
english_meaning: short-tempered; quick to lose one's temper (colloquial Cantonese)
explanation_mandarin: 「炮仗頸」是廣東話口語，形容人性情急躁、容易發火，好像炮仗一炸就爆，通常指爆發快但有時亦平息得快。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term describing someone who is quick-tempered or easily provoked—like a firecracker that explodes suddenly; often implies short, explosive outbursts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係有炮仗頸，成日為啲微細嘢發火。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 jau5 paau3 zoeng6 geng2, seng4 jat6 wai6 di1 mei4 sai3 je5 faat3 fo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真的很容易发脾气，经常为一些小事生气。
examples.english_sentence: He really has a short fuse; he often gets angry over small things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 遇到塞車，老細唔好做炮仗頸，冷靜處理就得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu6 dou3 sak1 ce1, lou5 sai3 m4 hou2 zou6 paau3 zoeng6 geng2, laang5 zing6 cyu2 lei5 zau6 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 遇到塞车，老板别发脾气，冷静处理就行了。
examples.english_sentence: When there's traffic, the boss shouldn't lose his temper; handling it calmly is fine.

mandarin_meaning: 指沒有戀愛關係、以性為主要目的的性伴侶（俚語）
english_meaning: friends with benefits; a casual sexual partner without romantic commitment
explanation_mandarin: 「炮友」是粵語俗語，指雙方主要以性為互動內容、而不打算發展成正式戀愛或穩定關係的伴侶。通常用於非正式或口語場合，帶有輕鬆或功利性的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term for a partner with whom one has primarily sexual relations without romantic commitment or plans for a serious relationship. Used informally and often implies a casual arrangement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話佢而家淨係想搵個炮友，唔想認真拍拖。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 keoi5 ji4 gaa1 zing6 hai6 soeng2 wan2 go3 paau3 jau5, m4 soeng2 jing6 zan1 paak3 to1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她說他/她現在只想找個炮友，不想認真交往。
examples.english_sentence: He/she says they only want to find a friends-with-benefits right now and don't want a serious relationship.

mandarin_meaning: 炮台 (pào tái)：放置火炮的土石或砌築構造，指作為防禦或攻擊用途的砲位、砲臺或火砲陣地；亦可泛指昔日軍事遺構。
english_meaning: gun battery; artillery emplacement; gun platform — a fortified position or structure where cannons or artillery are placed, often part of coastal or fortress defenses; also refers to historical military remains.
explanation_mandarin: 「炮台」通常指設置大砲或火砲的固定陣地或構築物，多見於海防或城防工事，現亦常作為歷史古蹟或旅遊景點保留。
explanation_english: “炮台” refers to a fixed emplacement or structure for mounting cannons/artillery, commonly used in coastal or fortress defenses; today such sites are often preserved as historical monuments or tourist attractions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個舊炮台而家係一個好受歡迎嘅旅遊景點。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 gau6 paau3 toi4 ji4 gaa1 hai6 jat1 go3 hou2 sau6 fun1 jing4 ge3 leoi5 jau4 ging2 dim2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个旧炮台现在是一个很受欢迎的旅游景点。
examples.english_sentence: This old battery is now a very popular tourist attraction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 清朝嗰陣呢度曾經有座炮台用嚟保護海港。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cing1 ciu4 go2 zan6 ni1 dou6 cang4 ging1 jau5 zo6 paau3 toi4 jung6 lai4 bou2 wu6 hoi2 gong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 清朝那时这里曾经有座炮台用来保护海港。
examples.english_sentence: During the Qing dynasty there used to be a battery here protecting the harbor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 軍方喺山頭重修一個炮台，變成觀景台同埋博物館一部分。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gwan1 fong1 hai2 saan1 tau4 cung4 sau1 jat1 go3 paau3 toi4, bin3 sing4 gun1 ging2 toi4 tung4 maai4 bok3 mat6 gun2 jat1 bou6 fan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 军方在山头重修一个炮台，变成观景台并成为博物馆的一部分。
examples.english_sentence: The military rebuilt a battery on the hilltop, which has become a viewing platform and part of a museum.

mandarin_meaning: 炮台山（地名），香港島上的一個地區，亦為港鐵一個車站名稱
english_meaning: Fortress Hill (a neighborhood on Hong Kong Island); also an MTR station name
explanation_mandarin: 炮台山位於香港島北岸，接近北角與銅鑼灣，港鐵港島線設有炮台山站，為區內重要交通樞紐與地名。
explanation_english: Fortress Hill is an area on the north shore of Hong Kong Island near North Point and Causeway Bay. There is an MTR station called Fortress Hill on the Island Line; the name refers both to the neighborhood and the station.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺炮台山站落車。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 pou3 toi4 saan1 zaam6 lok6 ce1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在炮台山站下车。
examples.english_sentence: I got off at Fortress Hill station.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚去炮台山食飯，你要一齊嗎？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 heoi3 pou3 toi4 saan1 sik6 faan6, nei5 jiu3 jat1 cai4 maa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚去炮台山吃饭，你要一起吗？
examples.english_sentence: I'm going to Fortress Hill to eat tonight — do you want to join?

mandarin_meaning: 炮口、炮管的尖端；（俚語）粗俗地指男性生殖器的龜頭
english_meaning: the muzzle/tip of a cannon or gun; (slang, vulgar) the glans/head of the male genitals
explanation_mandarin: 1) 指火炮或槍械等的出射端、炮口尖端。2) 在口語俚語中，有時粗俗地用來指男性生殖器的龜頭，用法不雅。
explanation_english: 1) Refers to the muzzle or tip of a cannon or firearm. 2) In colloquial slang it can be used vulgarly to refer to the glans of the male genitalia; this usage is impolite.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 大炮嘅炮尖冒出濃煙，戰場一片混亂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daai6 paau3 ge3 paau3 zim1 mou6 ceot1 nung4 jin1, zin3 coeng4 jat1 pin3 wan6 lyun6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 大炮的炮尖冒出浓烟，战场一片混乱。
examples.english_sentence: The cannon's muzzle emitted thick smoke; the battlefield was in chaos.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺口語裡，有人會粗俗咁用「炮尖」嚟指男性生殖器嘅龜頭，唔適合正式場合。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 hau2 jyu5 leoi5, jau5 jan4 wui5 cou1 suk6 gam2 jung6 "paau3 zim1" lei4 zi2 naam4 sing3 saang1 zik6 hei3 ge3 gwai1 tau4, m4 sik1 hap6 zing3 sik1 coeng4 hap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在口语中，有人会粗俗地用“炮尖”来指男性生殖器的龟头，不适合正式场合。
examples.english_sentence: In colloquial speech, some people vulgarly use '炮尖' to refer to the glans of the male genitals; it's not appropriate in formal settings.

mandarin_meaning: 炮弹 (pào dàn)
english_meaning: artillery shell; projectile; explosive shell
explanation_mandarin: 炮彈是軍事用語，指由火炮或砲兵發射的彈體，通常含有爆炸裝藥，用於攻擊或摧毀目標。
explanation_english: An artillery shell — a projectile fired from a cannon or artillery piece, usually containing explosive charge and used to attack or destroy targets.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 戰場上用炮彈攻擊敵方陣地。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zin3 coeng4 soeng6 jung6 paau3 daan6 gung1 gik1 dik6 fong1 zan6 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 战场上用炮弹攻击敌方阵地。
examples.english_sentence: On the battlefield, artillery shells are used to attack the enemy's positions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 那顆炮彈還沒爆，快撤離！
examples.jyutping_sentence: naa5 fo1 paau3 daan6 waan4 mei6 baau3, faai3 cit3 lei4!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那颗炮弹还没爆，快撤离！
examples.english_sentence: That shell hasn't exploded yet — evacuate quickly!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 博物館展出了二戰時期的炮彈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bok3 mat6 gun2 zin2 ceot1 liu5 ji6 zin3 si4 kei4 dik1 paau3 daan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 博物馆展出了二战时期的炮弹。
examples.english_sentence: The museum displayed artillery shells from World War II.

mandarin_meaning: 妓院；供性交易或約炮使用的房間
english_meaning: a brothel or a room used for sexual activity (often for prostitution or casual hookups)
explanation_mandarin: 「炮房」是廣東話俗語，指用來進行性交易或約炮的房間或場所，常見於以鐘點租用或提供性服務的酒店/場所。
explanation_english: In Cantonese slang, "炮房" refers to a room or place used for sexual activity, often associated with prostitution or casual hookups (e.g., hourly rooms in hotels used for sex).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋上星期去咗炮房。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 soeng6 sing1 kei4 heoi3 zo2 pou3 fong4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们上星期去了炮房。
examples.english_sentence: They went to a brothel/sex room last week.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽講嗰間酒店有炮房，係多人去約炮用嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 gong2 go2 gaan1 zau2 dim3 jau5 pou3 fong4, hai6 do1 jan4 heoi3 joek3 pou3 jung6 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 听说那间酒店有炮房，很多人去约炮用的。
examples.english_sentence: I heard that hotel has rooms used for hookups; many people go there to hook up.

mandarin_meaning: 炮楼（防御用的炮台或碉楼）
english_meaning: gun tower; fortified tower or battery (a fortified structure equipped for cannon/firepower)
explanation_mandarin: 指用于安装火炮或作为防御、瞭望的加固建筑，常见于沿海或要塞区域；亦可泛指旧时的碉楼或防御工事。
explanation_english: A fortified tower or battery designed to mount cannons or serve as a defensive/watch structure, commonly found in coastal or strategic locations; can also refer generally to historic watchtowers or fortifications.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰座炮樓係清朝用嚟防禦海盜嘅炮台。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 zo6 paau3 lau4 hai6 cing1 ciu4 jung6 lai4 fong4 jyu6 hoi2 dou6 ge3 paau3 toi4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那座炮楼是清朝用来防御海盗的炮台。
examples.english_sentence: That gun tower was used in the Qing dynasty as a battery to defend against pirates.

mandarin_meaning: 炮火（砲火、火炮射擊）；比喻猛烈的攻擊或抨擊
english_meaning: artillery fire; figuratively a barrage or heavy attack (e.g. criticism)
explanation_mandarin: 原指軍事上砲兵發射的火力；引申為集中且猛烈的攻擊、批評或攻勢。
explanation_english: Literally the fire from artillery; metaphorically used for a concentrated, intense attack or barrage (often of criticism or verbal attacks).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 前線嘅炮火好猛烈，居民要撤離。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cin4 sin3 ge3 paau3 fo2 hou2 ming5 lit6, geoi1 man4 jiu3 cit3 lei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 前线的炮火很猛烈，居民要撤离。
examples.english_sentence: The artillery fire at the front is intense; residents must evacuate.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一出事就俾媒體同網民一輪炮火轟嚟，壓力好大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 ceot1 si6 zau6 bei2 mui4 tai2 tung4 mong5 man4 jat1 leon4 paau3 fo2 hung1 lai4, aat3 lik6 hou2 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一出事就被媒体和网民一轮炮火轰击，压力很大。
examples.english_sentence: Once he got into trouble, he was bombarded by a barrage of criticism from the media and netizens, and the pressure was huge.

mandarin_meaning: 炮灰（pào huī）：被利用或犧牲的人、犧牲品
english_meaning: cannon fodder; an expendable person used as a sacrificial pawn
explanation_mandarin: 比喻在政治、軍事、職場等情境中被當作犧牲者或任人利用、地位卑微且無足輕重的人。
explanation_english: A figurative term for someone treated as expendable — a sacrificial pawn used or sacrificed in political struggles, workplaces, wars, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺嗰場政治鬥爭入面，佢淪為炮灰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 go2 coeng4 zing3 zi6 dau3 zang1 jap6 min6, keoi5 leon4 wai4 paau3 fui1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在那场政治斗争中，他沦为炮灰。
examples.english_sentence: He became cannon fodder in that political struggle.

mandarin_meaning: 炮烙（古代酷刑，用烙火烤人或以灼熱器具施刑）
english_meaning: pao luo (an ancient form of torture by roasting/scorching); roasting torture
explanation_mandarin: 「炮烙」指古代一種殘酷的刑罰或施刑方法，常以高溫灼烤致人受刑或致死。亦可引申形容極為嚴酷的懲罰。
explanation_english: ''Pao luo'' refers to an ancient cruel form of punishment involving roasting or scorching victims with heat. It can also be used figuratively to describe extremely severe punishment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 古代嘅酷刑有炮烙，聽落就嚇死人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gu2 doi6 ge3 huk6 jing4 jau5 paau3 lok3, teng1 lok6 zau6 haak3 sei2 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 古代的酷刑有炮烙，聽起來就嚇人。
examples.english_sentence: One of the brutal punishments in ancient times was pao luo (roasting); it sounds terrifying.

mandarin_meaning: 炮竹（pào zhú），即鞭炮、爆竹
english_meaning: firecrackers
explanation_mandarin: 指以火藥製成、燃放時會爆響的物品，通常在節慶（如春節）使用以慶祝或驅邪。
explanation_english: Refers to items made with gunpowder that explode with a loud bang when lit; commonly used in festivals (e.g., Lunar New Year) for celebration and to ward off evil.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新年期間，街上到處都有放炮竹，好熱鬧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 kei4 gaan1, gaai1 soeng6 dou3 cyu3 dou1 jau5 fong3 paau3 zuk1, hou2 jit6 naau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 過年期間，街上到處都有放炮竹，很熱鬧。
examples.english_sentence: During the New Year period, firecrackers are set off all over the streets; it's very lively.

mandarin_meaning: 膽大、魯莽（俚語）
english_meaning: gutsy; reckless; brazen (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 口語或俚語，常用於粵語，形容人膽子很大、做事魯莽或不顧後果。有時帶有貶義或警告意味。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang term describing someone who is very bold or reckless, acting without regard for consequences. Can be used disapprovingly or as a warning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係炮膽，乜嘢都敢試。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 paau3 daam2, mat1 je5 dou1 gam2 si3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是膽子大，什麼都敢試。
examples.english_sentence: He's really gutsy; he'll try anything.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁炮膽，唔驚會出事咩？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 paau3 daam2, m4 ging1 wui5 ceot1 si6 me1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這麼膽大，不怕會出事嗎？
examples.english_sentence: You're so reckless — aren't you afraid something might go wrong?

mandarin_meaning: 炮製 (pào zhì)：編造、捏造（如炮製假新聞）；亦可指中藥等的加工處理。
english_meaning: to fabricate or concoct (e.g. fabricate news); also to process (medicinal herbs).
explanation_mandarin: 「炮製」可指捏造、編造事實或材料，使其看似真實；在中醫語境中，亦指對藥材進行加工處理以備使用。
explanation_english: “炮製” can mean to fabricate or concoct something so it appears true (e.g., fabricated news); in traditional Chinese medicine it refers to processing medicinal materials for use.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日炮製假新聞，令到大家好混亂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 paau3 zai3 gaa2 san1 man4, ling6 dou3 daai6 gaa1 hou2 wan6 lyun6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常炮製假新聞，讓大家很混亂。
examples.english_sentence: He often fabricates fake news, causing a lot of confusion.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲中藥炮製得好，先至有效。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 zung1 joek6 paau3 zai3 dak1 hou2, sin1 zi3 jau5 haau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些中藥炮製得好，才能有效。
examples.english_sentence: Those Chinese medicines are properly processed before they are effective.

mandarin_meaning: 炮轰（強烈批評、猛烈抨擊；原指用火炮轟擊）
english_meaning: to lambaste / to heavily criticize; (literally) to bombard with artillery
explanation_mandarin: 原指以火炮轟擊敵方，現多用作比喻，表示對某人或某事進行猛烈抨擊或公開批評，常見於新聞與社交媒體語境。
explanation_english: Originally means to bombard with artillery. Figuratively it is used to describe launching a fierce attack or heavy criticism against someone or something, commonly seen in news and social media contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 敵軍炮轟我哋嘅陣地。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dik6 gwan1 paau3 hong1 ngo5 dei6 ge3 zan6 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 敵軍炮轟了我們的陣地。
examples.english_sentence: The enemy bombarded our positions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺記者會上畀記者炮轟，幾乎講唔出字來。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 gei3 ze2 wui6 soeng6 bei2 gei3 ze2 paau3 hong1, gei2 fu1 gong2 m4 ceot1 zi6 loi4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在記者會上被記者炮轟，幾乎說不出話來。
examples.english_sentence: He was lambasted by reporters at the press conference and could barely speak.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 大批網民喺社交媒體上炮轟嗰間公司，要求公開道歉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daai6 pat1 mong5 man4 hai2 se5 gaau1 mui4 tai2 soeng6 paau3 hong1 go2 gaan1 gung1 si1, jiu1 kau4 gung1 hoi1 dou6 hip3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 大量網民在社交媒體上炮轟那家公司，要求公開道歉。
examples.english_sentence: A large number of netizens bombarded the company on social media, demanding a public apology.

mandarin_meaning: 明亮；有神（常用於形容眼神）
english_meaning: bright; shining; (of eyes) bright and spirited
explanation_mandarin: 表示光亮、明亮或精神充沛，常用於詞語『炯炯有神』來形容人的眼神有神、精神飽滿。
explanation_english: Denotes brightness or shining quality; often used to describe lively, bright eyes (as in the idiom '炯炯有神').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢對住鏡頭炯炯有神，好有自信。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 deoi3 zyu6 geng3 tau4 gwing2 gwing2 jau5 san4, hou2 jau5 zi6 seon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他對著鏡頭炯炯有神，很有自信。
examples.english_sentence: He looked into the camera with bright, spirited eyes — very confident.

mandarin_meaning: 炯炯有神（形容眼睛明亮有神或精神奕奕）
english_meaning: lit. eyes bright and spirited; describes someone with bright, lively, or spirited eyes — looking energetic and alert
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容眼睛明亮、有神，或整體看起來精力充沛、精神很好。通常作為褒義描述外表氣色或眼神。
explanation_english: Describes bright, shining, and spirited eyes; often used to say someone looks lively, alert, or full of energy. Generally a complimentary expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢雙眼炯炯有神，望落好有精神。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng1 ngaan5 gwing2 gwing2 jau5 san4, mong6 lok6 hou2 jau5 zing1 san4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他雙眼炯炯有神，看起來很有精神。
examples.english_sentence: His eyes are bright and lively; he looks very energetic.

mandarin_meaning: 明亮、光明；鮮明、顯著（也常作人名用字）
english_meaning: bright; shining; clear; conspicuous (also commonly used in personal names)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容詞；也常用作人名用字
partOfSpeech_english: adjective; also used as a character in personal names
explanation_mandarin: 「炳」字本義為光明、明亮，引申為鮮明、顯著。現多見於書面語或用作人名中的字，表示光明、卓著或顯著的含義。
explanation_english: The character 炳 originally means bright or shining and by extension can mean clear or conspicuous. It is often seen in literary contexts and as a character in personal names, carrying the sense of brightness or distinction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢叫李炳強。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 giu3 lei5 bing2 koeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他叫李炳强。
examples.english_sentence: He is called Li Bingqiang.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢好炳，意思好清楚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 hou2 bing2, ji3 si1 hou2 cing1 co2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話很清晰，意思很清楚。
examples.english_sentence: He speaks very clearly; his meaning is easy to understand.

mandarin_meaning: （量詞/名詞）指一炷香；用於計算焚香的單位
english_meaning: a stick/piece of incense; a unit for counting an instance of burning incense
partOfSpeech_english: noun (can function as a measure word)
explanation_mandarin: 古字，常見於宗教或祭祀場景，表示一支香或一次焚香的量詞，如「一炷香」。
explanation_english: A classical character used to denote a single stick of incense or the unit for one burning of incense, commonly used in religious or ritual contexts (e.g. "one stick of incense").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺廟入面點咗一炷香，為屋企人祈福。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 miu6 jap6 min6 dim2 zo2 jat1 zyu3 hoeng1, wai4 uk1 kei5 jan4 kei4 fuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在廟裡點了一炷香，為家人祈福。
examples.english_sentence: He lit a stick of incense in the temple to pray for his family.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 拜祭嗰陣，大家都會燒幾炷香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: baai3 zai3 go2 zan6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 wui5 siu1 gei2 zyu3 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 祭祀時，大家都會燒幾炷香。
examples.english_sentence: During the ritual, everyone burns a few sticks of incense.

mandarin_meaning: 炸（zhá/zhà）：1. 用油高温烹调，油炸；2. 爆炸、炸裂；3. 口语中作夸张用，表示非常、强烈（如“笑到炸”）
english_meaning: to deep-fry; to explode/pop; colloquially, to be extremely/overwhelmed (e.g., 'laugh until explode')
explanation_mandarin: 在粵語中，“炸”常用作動詞，表示用油炸食物；亦可表示爆裂、爆炸；在口語中有時作誇張用法，形容某種程度很強或被某事嚇/逗得很厲害。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '炸' is commonly a verb meaning to deep-fry food; it can also mean to explode or burst. Informally it is used as an emphatic/colloquial expression to indicate an extreme reaction (e.g., laughing or being shocked).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚炸咗啲雞翼，幫你留咗兩隻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 zaa3 zo2 di1 gai1 jik6, bong1 nei5 lau4 zo2 loeng5 zek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚炸了些鸡翅，幫你留了兩只。
examples.english_sentence: I deep-fried some chicken wings tonight and saved two for you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個氣球突然炸咗，嚇到我跳咗起身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 hei3 kau4 dak6 syun4 zaa3 zo2, haak3 dou3 ngo5 tiu3 zo2 hei2 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 气球突然炸了，把我嚇得跳了起来。
examples.english_sentence: The balloon suddenly popped and scared me into jumping up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢套喜劇真係笑到炸，笑到唔停！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tou3 hei2 kek6 zan1 hai6 siu3 dou3 zaa3, siu3 dou3 m4 ting4!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这部喜剧真是笑到要爆了，笑个不停！
examples.english_sentence: This comedy is absolutely hilarious — I couldn't stop laughing!

mandarin_meaning: 出賣；背叛
english_meaning: to sell someone out; to betray
explanation_mandarin: 香港口語俚語，形容在關鍵時刻出賣或背叛同伴、隊友或信任你的人。常用於抱怨有人在重要時刻洩密或倒戈。
explanation_english: Hong Kong slang meaning to sell someone out or betray them at a critical moment. Often used to complain that someone leaked information or switched sides when trust was needed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺關鍵時刻炸両，出賣咗我哋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gwaan1 gin3 si4 hak1 zaa3 loeng5, ceot1 maai6 zo2 ngo5 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在關鍵時刻出賣了我們。
examples.english_sentence: He sold us out at a critical moment.

mandarin_meaning: 炸两（肠粉包油条）
english_meaning: Rice noodle roll (cheung fun) wrapped around a fried dough stick (youtiao); a common Cantonese breakfast/dim sum item
explanation_mandarin: 廣式點心／早餐：以腸粉包裹油條（炸麵條），常見於香港茶餐廳或點心店，通常配豆漿或醬油吃。
explanation_english: A Cantonese breakfast/dim sum dish where a deep-fried dough stick (youtiao) is wrapped inside a rice noodle roll (cheung fun). Commonly eaten at cha chaan tengs and dim sum restaurants, often served with soy milk or soy sauce.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我朝早食咗一份炸兩，幾好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 sik6 zo2 jat1 fan6 zaa3 loeng5, gei2 hou2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我早上吃了一份炸两，很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: I had a serving of zha liang this morning; it was quite tasty.

mandarin_meaning: 炸子鸡（广东/香港式整只或块状油炸、外皮酥脆的鸡）
english_meaning: Cantonese-style deep-fried chicken (often a whole chicken) with crispy skin
explanation_mandarin: 炸子雞是廣東／香港常見的一種做法，通常把整隻或切塊的雞以油炸或先炸後烤，令外皮非常酥脆、肉質多汁，常見於酒樓或燒臘店。
explanation_english: A Cantonese/Hong Kong specialty: a whole or portioned chicken deep-fried (or deep-fried then roasted) to produce very crispy skin and juicy meat. Commonly found in restaurants and roast shops.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚買隻炸子雞返屋企食啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 maai5 zek3 zaa3 zi2 gai1 faan1 uk1 kei2 sik6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚买一只炸子鸡回家吃吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's buy a fried chicken to take home and eat tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間酒樓嘅炸子雞皮特別脆，值得一試。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 zau2 lau4 ge3 zaa3 zi2 gai1 pei4 dak6 bit6 seoi3, zik6 dak1 jat1 si3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家酒楼的炸子鸡皮特别脆，值得一试。
examples.english_sentence: This restaurant's fried chicken has especially crispy skin—worth trying.

mandarin_meaning: 炸子鸡（广东式脆皮或整只油炸鸡）
english_meaning: Cantonese-style deep-fried whole chicken (crispy-skinned fried chicken)
explanation_mandarin: 指廣東／香港常見的一種炸整隻或脆皮雞，外皮酥脆、內裡多汁，常在酒樓或小吃店供應，屬粵菜特色之一。
explanation_english: Refers to a Cantonese-style deep-fried (often whole) chicken with crispy skin and juicy meat, commonly served in restaurants and eateries as part of Cantonese cuisine.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚去食炸子雞啦，聽講嗰間好正。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 heoi3 sik6 zaa3 zi2 gai1 laa1, teng1 gong2 go2 gaan1 hou2 zeng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们今晚去吃炸子鸡吧，听说那家很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go eat fried (whole) chicken tonight; I heard that place is really good.

mandarin_meaning: 炸弹 (zhàdàn)
english_meaning: bomb; explosive device; (figuratively) bombshell or a flop (e.g., box-office bomb)
explanation_mandarin: 1) 指用來爆炸的裝置或武器。2) 比喻突如其來、具重大影響的消息或事件（炸彈性消息）；也可用來形容失敗的作品或演出，例如「票房炸彈」。
explanation_english: 1) An explosive device or weapon. 2) Figuratively, a sudden, disruptive, high-impact piece of news (a 'bombshell'); can also refer to a failure (e.g., a box-office bomb).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方發現咗一個炸彈，已經封鎖咗現場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 fong1 faat3 jin4 zo2 jat1 go3 zaa3 daan6, ji5 ging1 fung1 so2 zo2 jin6 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方發現了一枚炸彈，已經封鎖現場。
examples.english_sentence: The police discovered a bomb and have sealed off the scene.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢拋咗個炸彈，話要辭職，大家都好震驚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 paau1 zo2 go3 zaa3 daan6, waa6 jiu3 ci4 zik1, daai6 gaa1 dou1 hou2 zan3 ging1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他拋下一個震撼消息，說要辭職，大家都很震驚。
examples.english_sentence: He dropped a bombshell saying he was going to resign; everyone was shocked.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢套戲票房成績太差，簡直係一個炸彈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tou3 hei3 piu3 fong4 sing4 zik1 taai3 caa1, gaan2 zik6 hai6 jat1 go3 zaa3 daan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這部電影票房慘淡，簡直是個炸彈。
examples.english_sentence: The movie flopped at the box office; it was a total bomb.

mandarin_meaning: 手殘；笨拙、不靈活（俗語）
english_meaning: clumsy; lacking skill (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，形容一個人手腳不靈巧或技術差，常用於打機或需要手工操作的情況。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang meaning someone is clumsy or lacks skill, often used for gaming or manual tasks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我打機好炸手，成日輸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 daa2 gei1 hou2 zaa3 sau2, seng4 jat6 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我打游戏很笨，总是输。
examples.english_sentence: I'm terrible at the game; I always lose.

mandarin_meaning: （設備）死機／崩潰
english_meaning: to crash (device or system); to disconnect/freeze (especially electronics or online games)
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俚語，字面意為「機器爆炸」，實際用來形容電子設備或系統突然停止運作、當機或大量使用者斷線。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term literally meaning "machine explodes." It is used to describe an electronic device or system crashing, freezing, or disconnecting (often used for phones, computers, or online games/servers).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我部電話又炸機喇，重開機先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 bou6 din6 waa2 jau6 zaa3 gei1 laa3, cung4 hoi1 gei1 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的手機又死機了，要先重開機。
examples.english_sentence: My phone crashed again; I need to restart it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚打機嗰陣，成隊人因為lag炸機晒，全部人都掉線。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 daa2 gei1 go2 zan6, seng4 deoi2 jan4 jan1 wai6 lag6 zaa3 gei1 saai3, cyun4 bou6 jan4 dou1 diu6 sin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚打遊戲時因為延遲整隊人都掉線了。
examples.english_sentence: When we were gaming tonight, the whole team got disconnected because of lag.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個系統一更新就有機會炸機，IT部話要修補。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 hai6 tung2 jat1 geng1 san1 zau6 jau5 gei1 wui6 zaa3 gei1, IT bou6 waa6 jiu3 sau1 bou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 系統一更新就有可能會崩潰，IT 部門說要修補。
examples.english_sentence: The system may crash every time it updates; IT said they'll patch it.

mandarin_meaning: 炸毁；用爆炸摧毁（某物）
english_meaning: to blow up; to destroy by explosion
explanation_mandarin: 用炸藥或爆炸力將建築、設施或其他物體破壞或毀滅。
explanation_english: To destroy or demolish something by explosion, typically using explosives or a bomb.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 昨晚嗰幢樓俾炸毀咗，仲有幾個人受傷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zok6 maan5 go2 zong6 lau4 bei2 zaa3 wai2 zo2, zung6 jau5 gei2 go3 jan4 sau6 soeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 昨晚那幢樓被炸毀了，還有幾個人受傷。
examples.english_sentence: That building was blown up last night; several people were injured.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋嘗試用炸藥炸毀條橋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 soeng4 si3 jung6 zaa3 joek6 zaa3 wai2 tiu4 kiu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們試圖用炸藥炸毀那座橋。
examples.english_sentence: They attempted to blow up the bridge with explosives.

mandarin_meaning: （網路用語）刷屏、爆紅，指帖子或內容在短時間內被大量評論、分享或出現在使用者動態上；也可指在群組或討論區連續發很多訊息以刷屏
english_meaning: to go viral / to flood the feed / to spam (a chat/thread) — a slang verb describing a post or content receiving a huge amount of responses or appearances in a short time, or someone repeatedly posting to spam the feed
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語網絡俗語。當一則帖文或內容在短時間內被大量留言、按讚、分享或被不斷轉發，導致討論版面被大量訊息佔據，便稱之為「炸版」。亦可指有人刻意連續發訊息刷屏。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese internet slang verb. It describes a post or content that suddenly attracts a large number of comments/shares/likes in a short time (i.e., goes viral or floods the thread), or the act of repeatedly posting to spam or dominate a feed/group.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個帖短時間內炸版，留言多到數唔晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 tip3 dyun2 si4 gaan1 noi6 zaa3 baan2, lau4 jim4 do1 dou3 sou3 m4 saat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個帖在短時間內炸版（刷屏），留言多到數不清。
examples.english_sentence: This post went viral in a short time — there were so many comments I couldn't count them all.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日喺群組度炸版，會令人厭煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 seng4 jat6 hai2 kwan4 zou2 dou6 zaa3 baan2, wui5 ling6 jan4 jim6 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要老是在群組裡刷屏，會讓人感到厭煩。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep spamming the group chat — it annoys people.
